1.1.9 — Passwords, and a steadier Glance

  • A built-in password manager: Pane offers to save passwords when you sign in, suggests your saved logins right under the field (Touch ID to fill), and suggests strong passwords on sign-up forms. Passwords live in your Mac's Keychain. Manage them, or import a CSV from another browser, in Settings › Passwords.
  • Closing a tab playing video now stops it right away — no more video carrying on or popping out in picture in picture after the tab is gone.
  • Glance: closing it stops the page at once, moving a page to the browser is smoother, and downloads and Save As work there too.
  • Closed tabs no longer keep running in the background, so Pane uses less memory over time.

1.1.8 — Snappier

  • Tabs you're not looking at now rest, like in Safari, so the tab you're on gets the whole machine — smoother scrolling, less battery. Switching back is still instant.
  • Pages show up sooner: Pane now knows the moment a page first draws instead of checking for it.

1.1.7 — A new welcome, a new icon

  • A brand-new full-screen welcome: a living gradient that follows your pointer, colors you can try across the whole screen, and shortcuts you can press to learn. See it any time from Help › Show Welcome.
  • A new app icon.
